data_schema.title: USDA Directive Extraction Schema v2.1 (DR/DM)
data_schema.description: Extracts metadata and structured policy statements from 3000 series USDA Departmental Regulation (DR) or Departmental Manual (DM). Governing rules: (1) Any field described as verbatim must be copied character-for-character from the source document. Never paraphrase, merge, abbreviate, summarize, or insert ellipses. (2) Do not infer. If the source does not support an optional field, leave the field out entirely. Never return an empty string or a guess. (3) Only the label fields in policy_statements (statement_kind, statement_function, modal_use, normative_force, actor_basis) are interpretations. Every other field is quoted or copied from the document.

document_type.description: Type of document as printed in the header, such as 'Departmental Regulation' or 'Departmental Manual'.

issuing_organization.description: Organization issuing the document, verbatim from the header.

issuing_location.description: Location of the issuing organization, verbatim from the header.

regulation_number.description: Official document number from the header, verbatim, for example 'DR 3105-001'.

subject.description: Subject or title of the document, verbatim from the header.

issue_date.description: Issue date from the header, as written.

expiration_date.description: Expiration date from the header, as written. Leave out if none is printed.

opi.description: Office of Primary Interest (OPI) from the header, verbatim.

supersedes.description: The prior document this document supersedes. Take all values from the supersession paragraph in the body (usually under Special Instructions/Cancellations), NOT from the header. Leave the whole object out if the document supersedes nothing.

document_number.description: Number of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph. If it is identical to this document's own number, still copy it from the supersession paragraph, not the header.

document_title.description: Title of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

document_date.description: Date of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

scope.description: The text of the Scope section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Scope section.

purpose.description: The text of the Purpose section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Purpose section.

inquiries.description: Contact information from the Inquiries section. Leave out any property the document does not state; never return an empty string.

office.description: Office or division named for inquiries, verbatim. Leave out if the document names no office.

email.description: Email address given for inquiries, verbatim, without trailing punctuation. Leave out if none is given.

table_of_contents.description: Top-level entries of the printed table of contents, in order, including appendices. Return an empty list if the document prints no table of contents.

section_number.description: Section or appendix identifier as printed, for example '1.' or 'Appendix A'.

section_title.description: Section or appendix title as printed in the table of contents.

page.description: Page number exactly as printed in the table of contents, for example '2' or 'A-1'. Copy it even if the section actually starts on a different page. Leave out if no page number is printed.

actors.description: Registry of every distinct entity that the policy text names in an acting role. One entry per entity. Include every entity used as actor_name in policy_statements. Also include entities the document names in a role without being directed to act (mark those mentioned_only). Documents (bylaws, regulations, directives) are NEVER actors and must not appear here. Return an empty list if the document names no actors.

name.description: The entity's name exactly as written in the policy text, without a leading article ('the') and without a possessive. Keep a compound name intact if the document writes it as one phrase, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'. This is the join key used by actor_name in policy_statements, so spell it identically there.

components.description: ONLY for a name that joins separate entities with commas or 'and' (for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices' gives 'USDA Mission Areas', 'agencies', 'staff offices'). NEVER split a job title from the organization that qualifies it ('Director of IT, Office of the Inspector General' is ONE position), and never split an organization name from the position it modifies ('Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Associate CIOs (ACIO)' is ONE group). Each component is a verbatim substring of the name. Leave out for single entities.

items.description: One verbatim component of a compound actor name.

actor_type.description: Kind of entity. Use exactly one of: position (a job title, singular or plural, for example 'USDA CIO' or 'Mission Area Assistant CIOs'), office (an organizational unit, for example 'OCIO Executive Secretariat'), council_or_body (a council, committee, board, or similar body), group (a category of organizations or units, not job titles, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'), external_entity (an entity outside the document's authority), program_or_system (an IT initiative, system, program, or project that the document says must act or conform).

binding_status.description: bound_by_this_document: the document directs, permits, or assigns a function or role to this entity and has authority over it. mentioned_only: the document names the entity but cannot or does not impose anything on it (for example a council or agency outside USDA that the document says a USDA body partners with).

policy_statements.description: Structured statements from the numbered body sections only (not the table of contents, not the appendices). RULES. (a) SENTENCES: emit one statement per sentence. If a paragraph has more than one sentence, give each its own statement with ids suffixed .s1, .s2, and so on. Abbreviations and legal citations ('U.S.C.', 'CFR', '§', 'et seq.') do not end a sentence. (b) LISTS: when text introduces a list (usually ends with a colon, for example 'The USDA CIO will:'), emit the introducing text as one statement with statement_kind 'lead_in', and emit EVERY item of the list as its own statement with statement_kind 'list_item' and parent_statement_id set to the id of the lead_in. Never skip list items, including lists of legal authorities. For a list inside a list, parent_statement_id is the immediate parent. (c) NEVER merge text from different sentences, paragraphs, or list items into one statement. (d) Copy text exactly; do not summarize. (e) PRONOUNS: when a sentence's subject is a pronoun ('It', 'Its', 'They') that refers to a named actor in the preceding sentence, resolve it: set actor_name to that actor and actor_basis to resolved_from_prior_sentence. (f) DOCUMENT AS SUBJECT: when the grammatical subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'), leave actor_name out; the entities the document acts on belong in target.

statement_id.description: Printed numbering path of the statement: section number, then paragraph letter, then item number in parentheses, for example '1', '3.a', '5.d.s2', '6.a(1)'. Add '.sN' only when a paragraph contains more than one sentence. Must be unique within the document.

statement_kind.description: standalone: a complete sentence that stands on its own. lead_in: text that introduces a list and is incomplete without its items. list_item: a list item that completes its lead_in.

parent_statement_id.description: Include ONLY when statement_kind is list_item: the statement_id of its immediate lead_in. For every other statement leave this field out entirely; never return an empty string.

section_number.description: Number of the section containing the statement, digits only, for example '6'.

section_title.description: Title of the section containing the statement, as shown in the table of contents, for example 'Roles and Responsibilities'.

source_text.description: VERBATIM text of this one sentence or list item exactly as printed, including trailing punctuation such as ':' or ';' and including any list-ending words such as 'and'. No paraphrase, no ellipses, no text from any other statement. For a list_item, give only the item's own text, not the lead_in.

statement_function.description: What the statement does. obligation: a required action or compliance requirement on an actor. responsibility: a standing duty or function assigned to an actor, including present-tense descriptions of what a body does. role_designation: assigns an entity to a role, for example membership or voting status. authority: names a legal source of authority or a grant of authority. scope: states what or whom the document applies to. purpose: states why the document or a body exists. definition: defines a term. condition: states a standalone triggering condition. exception: carves out an exception. savings_clause: states that the document does not displace existing authorities or delegations. effectivity: states when the document takes effect or how long it lasts. supersession: states that the document replaces another. classification_rule: states a rule that classifies something or applies a requirement when a status is met. reference: points to another document or location. inquiry: tells who may be contacted. container: use for every lead_in statement. other: none of the above.

modal_verb.description: The modal word or phrase of the statement's MAIN clause, exactly as written, for example 'will', 'can', 'may', 'must', 'shall', 'must not'. Ignore modals inside relative or subordinate clauses (for 'advises the USDA CIO on IT matters that may become IT investments', the 'may' is not the statement's modal). For a list_item whose own text has no modal, copy the modal from its lead_in. Leave out if the main clause has no modal.

modal_use.description: deontic: the main-clause modal directs, permits, or prohibits action by an actor (for example 'The Deputy CIO will serve', 'can direct questions'). predictive: the modal only states what will happen or remain true (for example 'It will remain in effect until superseded'). none: the main clause has no modal.

normative_force.description: mandatory: deontic 'will', 'shall', or 'must' directing an actor to act or to serve in a role. prohibitive: deontic 'must not', 'shall not', or 'may not'. permissive: deontic 'may' or 'can'. assigned: a present-tense statement with no deontic modal that assigns or describes a function, duty, or role of a named actor (for example 'The CIO Council advises the USDA CIO on...', 'It assesses the needs of...'); use it only when actor_name is present, and never for purpose statements. descriptive: everything else with no deontic force, including purpose, scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, references, authorities, definitions, and statements about the document itself or about other documents. not_applicable: use for every lead_in; its force is carried by its list_items.

actor_name.description: The entity directed to act, permitted to act, or assigned a function or role by this statement, spelled exactly as in the matching actors[].name. It must appear in source_text or in the lead_in's text (leading article removed); for a resolved pronoun, copy it from the antecedent sentence. Leave out when the statement binds no actor: scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, statements about documents (including bylaws), and any statement whose subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'). Never supply an actor that is not stated in the text or resolvable from the preceding sentence. Always leave out for lead_in statements.

actor_basis.description: Include ONLY when actor_name is present; otherwise leave this field out entirely. explicit_in_statement: the actor appears in this statement's own source_text. inherited_from_lead_in: the actor appears only in the lead_in that this list_item completes. resolved_from_prior_sentence: the subject is a pronoun resolved to the actor named in the preceding sentence.

target.description: VERBATIM phrase naming what the action is directed at or what the statement applies to, starting at the first word after any leading article ('a', 'an', 'the'). For a role_designation, the body or unit the role is within (for example 'CIO Council'). Leave out if none.

resulting_status.description: VERBATIM phrase naming the status or role that a role_designation or classification_rule confers, for example 'voting member' or 'advisory (non-voting) members'. Leave out for other statements.

conditions.description: VERBATIM phrases that restrict when or to what the statement applies, for example 'that the CIO Council designates as enterprise initiatives'. Do NOT treat a non-restrictive descriptive phrase set off by commas (for example 'appointed by the USDA CIO' in 'The Secretariat, appointed by the USDA CIO, will serve') as a condition. Leave out if there are none.

items.description: One verbatim condition phrase copied from source_text.

cross_references.description: Other documents, laws, or regulations cited in source_text, each copied verbatim as ONE entry per cited authority, including its code citation (for example 'The Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 11101 et seq.' is one entry; for a list_item that is just a citation, the entry is the item text without the trailing ';' or 'and'). Never add a separate entry for a title that is part of the same citation (the words 'Chief Information Officer' after '7 CFR § 2.32'). Never list generic categories such as 'law' or 'Federal regulation'. Leave out if none.

acronyms.description: Acronyms and abbreviations listed in the acronym appendix, one entry per row, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no acronym appendix.

acronym.description: Acronym or abbreviation exactly as printed.

authorities_and_references.description: Entries of the Authorities and References appendix, one per entry, each copied verbatim, including any date, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no such appendix.

items.description: One appendix entry exactly as printed, joined across line breaks.

policy_statements.source_text: This Departmental Regulation (DR) establishes the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Information Technology (IT) Security Controls Baselines for information systems.

The USDA derives IT security baselines (ITSB) from the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Special Publication (SP) 800-53B, Control Baselines for Information Systems and Organizations, listing of controls and control enhancements assigned to NIST SP 800-53, Revision 5, Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations, security control families.
cross_references: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Special Publication (SP) 800-53B, Control Baselines for Information Systems and Organizations
NIST SP 800-53, Revision 5, Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations

policy_statements.target: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: This DR also instructs on tailoring security and privacy controls to protect USDA information systems against risks.
This DR applies to all:
USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, and personnel who work for or on behalf of USDA.

policy_statements.source_text: The term “USDA personnel” encompasses USDA employees, appointees, contractors, partners, interns, fellows, affiliates, and volunteers;
Federal information, per DR 3080-001, Records Management, in any medium or form generated, collected, provided, transmitted, stored, maintained, or accessed by or on behalf of USDA; and

Information systems or services (including cloud-based services) used or operated by USDA, contractors, or other organizations on behalf of or funded by USDA, and interconnections between or among systems or services.
policy_statements.target: Information systems or services (including cloud-based services)

policy_statements.source_text: Nothing in this policy alters the requirements for protecting national security systems or information.

policy_statements.source_text: This policy follows NIST SP 800-53B.
The requirements for security and privacy controls derive from applicable laws, Executive Orders (E.O.), directives, regulations, policies, standards, and mission needs.

Security controls are policies, procedures, and technical configurations which an organization implements on their information systems to protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information.
Privacy controls ensure compliance with relevant privacy requirements, and manage privacy risks.
Control baselines are a collection of controls assembled to address the protection needs of a group, organization, or community of interest.
The selection, design, and effective implementation of controls are important tasks that can impact an organization’s assets and operations, and the welfare of individuals and the Nation.
NIST SP 800-37, Revision 2, defines two approaches for the selection of security and privacy controls: a baseline control selection, and a tailored control selection.
Tailored controls may also be called overlays.

Overlays complement the NIST control baselines by providing an opportunity to add or eliminate controls to accommodate organizational requirements, while continuing to protect information proportionate to risk.
Organizations can use overlays to customize control baselines by describing control applicability and providing interpretations for specific technologies.
This USDA ITSB policy will assist system owners in establishing ITSB and creating tailored security and privacy control baselines for their specific information systems.
System owners must align risk management practices defined in NIST SP 800-37, Revision 2 to effectively manage their security and privacy risks.
policy_statements.target: risk management practices defined in NIST SP 800-37, Revision 2

policy_statements.source_text: ITSB and overlays aid system owners to select the baseline controls for their specific information system logical boundary through the following:
Categorize the information system boundary, and document the system description using the following:
System design with required documentation;
Systems supporting RMF roles;
Boundary authorization information;
Document the type of information, typical usage (e.g., stored, accessed, or processed), and the potential impact should a compromise of confidentiality, integrity, or availability occur.
policy_statements.target: type of information, typical usage (e.g., stored, accessed, or processed), and the potential impact should a compromise of confidentiality, integrity, or availability occur

policy_statements.source_text: Base this security categorization on the high watermark of information type impact levels.

Use Federal Information Processing Standards Publication (FIPS PUB) 199, Standards for Security Categorization of Federal Information and Information Systems for security categorization for guidance; and
cross_references: Federal Information Processing Standards Publication (FIPS PUB) 199, Standards for Security Categorization of Federal Information and Information Systems

policy_statements.source_text: Review and document information stored, accessed, processed, or exchanged from USDA or relative external information system for identification of other possible sensitive information with the potential of raising the high watermark of the information system boundary.
policy_statements.target: information stored, accessed, processed, or exchanged from USDA or relative external information system

policy_statements.source_text: Select the baseline system security and privacy controls through the following:
Document the baseline controls applicable to NIST SP 800-53, Revision 5;
policy_statements.target: baseline controls applicable to NIST SP 800-53, Revision 5

policy_statements.source_text: Determine if there are privacy risks arising from processing personally identifiable information (PII).
If there are risks, then system owners must create a privacy control baseline in addition to security baseline controls.
conditions: If there are risks

policy_statements.source_text: NIST SP 800-53B explains the privacy controls in further detail.
The USDA Chief Information Officer (CIO), serving as the Senior Agency Official for Privacy (SAOP) oversees the management of privacy controls; and
Follow NIST SP 800-53, Revision 5 security controls for low, moderate, or high.
policy_statements.target: NIST SP 800-53, Revision 5 security controls for low, moderate, or high

policy_statements.source_text: System owners will review and follow control baseline assumptions through the following:
Ensure the information in organizational systems is persistent (e.g., days, weeks);
Determine if information systems are multi-user (either serially or concurrently) in operation;
Determine if information (e.g., controlled unclassified information (CUI)) requires additional access controls;
Determine if the information system resides in a networked environment, and is general purpose in nature;
Determine if USDA has provided the necessary structure, resources, and infrastructure to implement the controls; and
Determine if any of the above assumptions are not valid, then some of the security controls allocated to the control baseline may not apply.
System owners must tailor the security and privacy control baselines to align with the unique and specific circumstances of their information system boundary.
They must label each control and control enhancement through the following:
Document inherited common controls from the most recent SSP (within 12 months);
conditions: within 12 months

policy_statements.source_text: Document system-specific or hybrid security controls, per the most recent security assessment, and continuously monitored; and
Document known acceptance of risk:
The system’s Authorizing Official (AO) has lone authority to accept risks for required ITSB controls and policies, except for those explicitly requiring acceptance by the USDA CIO;
policy_statements.target: risks for required ITSB controls and policies
conditions: except for those explicitly requiring acceptance by the USDA CIO

policy_statements.source_text: Risk-based acceptance requests must document the following information:
A justification statement explaining the disregard of the control;
A statement explaining and describing which compensating controls they will use to reduce associated risks;
A risk statement describing all residual or new risk resulting from this decision; and
A plan of action and milestones (POA&M) for relevant unimplemented controls.
Render a risk decision where policy requires AO approval of risk, the rendered decision; and
Reference all risk-based acceptances in the relevant system security documentation (e.g., SSP, Risk Assessment) and made available to the USDA Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) upon request.
conditions: upon request

policy_statements.source_text: When controls in the initial baselines do not apply to every component in the system, system owners must work with the AO to make risk-based decisions on where to apply or allocate specific security controls to satisfy security and privacy requirements.
conditions: When controls in the initial baselines do not apply to every component in the system

policy_statements.source_text: System owners will follow scoping considerations when tailoring the security and privacy control baselines through the following:
Use overlays, which are the foundation for determining the needed set of system controls;

Tailor the baseline if operational and environmental factors diverge significantly from baseline assumptions, (i.e., a FISMA boundary is an application only hosted in the cloud), consider the following common environmental factors:
conditions: if operational and environmental factors diverge significantly from baseline assumptions

policy_statements.source_text: Mobile devices;
Single-user systems;
Bandwidth limitations;
Air-gapped systems;
Internet of Things devices;
Limited functionality systems (i.e., printers, digital cameras);
Systems processing, storing, or transmitting non-persistent information;
Application-only systems; and
Systems requiring public access.
Controls supporting only one or two of the security objectives may be downgraded to the corresponding control in a lower baseline.
policy_statements.target: Controls supporting only one or two of the security objectives

policy_statements.source_text: Modification or elimination of controls may be required if not defined in a lower baseline.
conditions: if not defined in a lower baseline

policy_statements.source_text: Downgrading a control must first reflect the FIPS PUB 199 security category for the supported security objectives.
policy_statements.target: FIPS PUB 199 security category for the supported security objectives

policy_statements.source_text: Then the downgrade must consider FIPS PUB 200, Minimum Security Requirements for Federal Information and Information Systems, impact level (i.e., high watermark).
cross_references: FIPS PUB 200, Minimum Security Requirements for Federal Information and Information Systems
policy_statements.target: FIPS PUB 200, Minimum Security Requirements for Federal Information and Information Systems, impact level (i.e., high watermark)

policy_statements.source_text: Downgrades must have an organizational risk assessment, and cannot adversely affect the level of protection for the security-relevant information within the system;
USDA does not allow use of controls whose implementation has the potential to degrade, debilitate, or interfere with USDA’s overall mission and business functions.
policy_statements.target: controls whose implementation has the potential to degrade, debilitate, or interfere with USDA’s overall mission and business functions

policy_statements.source_text: Decisions on the propriety of control implementation must always include legislative, regulatory, and policy requirements;
System owners will not tailor controls to meet legislative, regulatory, or policy requirements without the approval of the AO; and
conditions: without the approval of the AO

policy_statements.source_text: Tailoring will not arbitrarily remove security and privacy controls from baselines.
Tailoring decisions will be defensible based on mission and business needs, a sound rationale, and explicit risk-based determinations;
Designated controls (i.e., common, hybrid, or system-specific) allocated to the individual system elements (e.g., machine, physical, or human elements) must meet security and privacy requirements.
policy_statements.target: Designated controls (i.e., common, hybrid, or system-specific) allocated to the individual system elements (e.g., machine, physical, or human elements)

policy_statements.source_text: These controls must also:
Identify and implement compensating controls, approved by the AO, for any incompatible controls on the information system; and
Utilize risk assessment results to determine the sufficiency of controls in the tailored baseline.
The respective AO and Information System Security Manager (ISSM) must review and approve the determination.
policy_statements.actor_name: respective AO and Information System Security Manager (ISSM)

policy_statements.source_text: When instituting control tailoring, the system owners and the AO must work with their ISSM to provide complete implementation details for all controls employed on the system.
policy_statements.target: all controls employed on the system
conditions: When instituting control tailoring

policy_statements.source_text: They must also detail this information in the system's SSP, without exceptions.
System owners may tailor out controls with this guidance.
When choosing not to employ a control, the respective SSP documentation must contain all the following information without exception:
conditions: When choosing not to employ a control

policy_statements.source_text: A justification statement explaining the disregard of the control.
policy_statements.target: justification statement explaining the disregard of the control

policy_statements.source_text: Two acceptable reasons are the scoping guidance in NIST SP 800-53, Revision 5 prevents employment, and control implementation resulting in technical or operational incompatibility on a specific system;
A statement describing which compensating controls they will use to offset associated risks;
policy_statements.target: statement describing which compensating controls they will use to offset associated risks

policy_statements.source_text: A risk assessment describing all residual or new risks resulting from this decision; and
policy_statements.target: risk assessment describing all residual or new risks resulting from this decision

policy_statements.source_text: A POA&M for relevant, unimplemented controls.
System owners must meet all USDA compliance requirements including those established in this DR.
policy_statements.target: all USDA compliance requirements including those established in this DR

policy_statements.source_text: The Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Cybersecurity & Privacy Operations Center (CPOC) will ensure compliance by auditing and reviewing security and privacy control assessments of a sampling of systems based on this ITSB.
policy_statements.actor_name: Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Cybersecurity & Privacy Operations Center (CPOC)

policy_statements.source_text: These assessments will include a review of the controls baseline for a given system based on the system's FIPS PUB 199 impact level.
policy_statements.target: controls baseline for a given system

policy_statements.source_text: System owners will categorize the status of each control in the applicable baseline as:
Implemented and functioning effectively to provide a minimum level of security;
Implemented but not functioning effectively, with either a subsequent POA&M detailing steps to facilitate effective functioning, or the AO’s documented risk acceptance;
Not implemented, with supporting documentation as required; or
Other, with detailed explanation.
USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will document and analyze lessons learned on their programs, control activities, procedures, and tasks.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
policy_statements.target: lessons learned on their programs, control activities, procedures, and tasks

The requirements for security and privacy controls derive from applicable laws, Executive Orders (E.O.), directives, regulations, policies, standards, and mission needs.

Security controls are policies, procedures, and technical configurations which an organization implements on their information systems to protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information.
Privacy controls ensure compliance with relevant privacy requirements, and manage privacy risks.
Control baselines are a collection of controls assembled to address the protection needs of a group, organization, or community of interest.
The selection, design, and effective implementation of controls are important tasks that can impact an organization’s assets and operations, and the welfare of individuals and the Nation.
NIST SP 800-37, Revision 2, defines two approaches for the selection of security and privacy controls: a baseline control selection, and a tailored control selection.
Tailored controls may also be called overlays.

Overlays complement the NIST control baselines by providing an opportunity to add or eliminate controls to accommodate organizational requirements, while continuing to protect information proportionate to risk.
Organizations can use overlays to customize control baselines by describing control applicability and providing interpretations for specific technologies.
This USDA ITSB policy will assist system owners in establishing ITSB and creating tailored security and privacy control baselines for their specific information systems.
